title: Filter bar is shown below the tab row on the Work Orders page
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. At least a few work orders exist in the shop.
steps: 1. Open the Work Orders page.
2. Look at the area directly under the tab row (All, Estimates, Completed, My Work Orders).
expected: 1. A filter bar is visible directly below the tab row and above the work order table.
2. The filter bar is shown by default (expanded) without having to turn anything on.
notes: Placement (below tabs, above table) confirmed in the final design frame 11854:24657.

title: Five filter chips appear in a fixed order, each with an icon, its name and a down arrow
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the filter bar visible.
3. You are on the All tab (on the Estimates and Completed tabs the Status chip is shown greyed out and already filled in, so the chips do not all look the same there).
steps: 1. Read the filter chips in the filter bar from left to right.
2. Look at what each chip shows.
expected: 1. Exactly five filter chips appear, in this order: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site.
2. Each chip shows a small icon, the filter name and a down arrow (chevron) indicating it opens a dropdown.
3. In the design the icons are: a spinner for Status, a person for Customer, a wrench for Lead Technician, a headset for Service Advisor and a truck for Asset on site.
notes: WORDING REPAIR 2026-07-31 (Rule-28 audit FIX-WORDING, user-authorized): added precondition 3 'You are on the All tab' — the default landing tab is Estimates (FLT-TAB-06) where the Status chip renders greyed/pre-filled, so the five-identical-chips expectation only reads cleanly on the All tab. | DESIGN TYPO FLAG: the design's work order table column header reads 'Lead Tehnician' (missing 'c') while the filter chip itself is spelled correctly - the build must ship 'Lead Technician' everywhere (design-notes C.1); if the build inherits the typo, raise a bug. Chip label capitalisation 'Asset on site' (design) vs 'Asset on Site' (spec) - VIU-confirm the exact on-screen label.

title: The filter bar still shows the other four chips on the Estimates tab
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. Click the Estimates tab.
2. Look at the filter bar.
expected: 1. The filter bar is still shown - it does not disappear on this tab.
2. The Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor and Asset on site chips are all displayed and usable.
3. The Status chip is not usable on this tab: it is shown greyed out and already filled in with the tab's own status, and cannot be clicked.

notes: Status-chip wording standard: this behaviour is described as "shown greyed out, pre-filled, not clickable" everywhere in this suite. PRD v1.6 S9-R2/S9-R3/S2-N1/S2-N2/S1-N1 and §4 still say "hidden" - stale prose, Branko asked to align (item B1). Do not reintroduce the word "hidden". | Consistency fix 2026-07-31 (FIX-PLAN F1a, user-authorized) against spec v1.6 (Confluence v12, 2026-07-28). | (VIU-confirm the exact greyed-out look of the Status chip - flag kept here, out of the tester-facing text.)

title: Status chip opens a checkbox list of all nine work order statuses with a Clear selection action
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All or My Work Orders tab.
3. No filters are currently selected.
steps: 1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Read the list of options from top to bottom.
3. Look at the bottom of the dropdown panel.
expected: 1. A dropdown panel opens under the Status chip.
2. It lists all nine statuses as checkboxes, in this order: Estimate, Approved, In progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported.
3. All checkboxes are unticked (nothing selected yet).
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom of the dropdown.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 #6/#7 (11854:24280, 11854:24194 - option list also evidenced in the final mobile sheets #16/#17); requirements.md Story 2
notes: Design shows 'In progress' (lower-case p) while the spec writes 'In Progress' - VIU-confirm the exact on-screen capitalisation. The desktop dropdown popover frames are superseded as separate frames, but the 9-option list is fully evidenced in the final mobile sheets; capture the build's real desktop dropdown at VIU.

title: Ticking one status filters the table immediately, with no apply button
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in at least two different statuses (for example some Estimate and some Approved - create ZZAUTOTEST work orders if needed).
steps: 1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick the checkbox for one status (for example Estimate).
3. Watch the work order table while the dropdown is still open.
expected: 1. The ticked checkbox appears filled (checked).
2. The table updates immediately to show only work orders in the selected status - there is no confirm or apply button on desktop.
3. Work orders in other statuses are no longer listed.

title: Ticking several statuses shows work orders matching any of them
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in at least three different statuses (seed ZZAUTOTEST work orders if needed).
steps: 1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick two or more statuses (for example Estimate and Approved).
3. Look at the work order table.
expected: 1. Every ticked status shows a filled checkbox.
2. The table shows work orders whose status matches ANY of the ticked statuses (both Estimate and Approved rows appear).
3. Work orders in statuses that are not ticked are hidden.
4. There is no limit on how many statuses you can tick.
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; §4 Key Decisions (no selection limit)
notes: Tech plan 2026-07-29 (engineering intent - confirm live at the wording/behaviour pass): the Imported status may be MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the other statuses/filters (G1) - see FLT-STAT-07; pending Branko confirmation (spec S2-R1 lists it as a plain status).

title: Clear selection in the Status dropdown unticks every status and removes the filter
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Two or more statuses are ticked in the Status filter and the table is filtered.
steps: 1. Open the Status dropdown (if it is not already open).
2. Click 'Clear selection' at the bottom of the dropdown.
3. Look at the checkboxes and the table.
expected: 1. All status checkboxes become unticked.
2. The Status filter is removed and the table returns to showing work orders of every status.
3. Only the Status filter is affected - any other active filters stay applied.

title: Clicking outside the Status dropdown closes it and keeps the selections applied
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. The Status dropdown is open with at least one status ticked.
steps: 1. Click anywhere outside the open dropdown (for example on empty page space).
2. Look at the dropdown, the Status chip and the table.
expected: 1. The dropdown closes.
2. The ticked statuses stay selected - the Status chip stays in its active state showing the selection.
3. The table stays filtered by the selected statuses.

title: Selecting statuses that no work order has shows the empty state
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. At least one status exists that NO current work order has (for example Imported - check the list first).
steps: 1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick only the status that no work order currently has.
3. Look at the table area.
expected: 1. The table shows no rows.
2. An empty state is displayed saying no results were found for the current filters (see the Empty State cases for its full content).
3. The app does not show an error.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 (empty state not drawn in the final WO frames - message text to be captured from the build)
notes: Exact empty-state message text is not shown in the final design frames - VIU-confirm the real on-screen wording.

title: The toolbar funnel button collapses the filter bar and the table reclaims the space
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the filter bar visible (expanded).
steps: 1. Find the filter (funnel) icon button in the page toolbar (next to the Search magnifier and the column/layout toggle, left of the New Work Order button).
2. Click the funnel icon once.
3. Look at the filter bar area and the table.
expected: 1. The filter bar row is hidden.
2. The work order table moves up and uses the reclaimed vertical space.
3. The funnel icon shows a pressed/active look while the bar is collapsed.

title: Expanding the filter bar brings it back exactly as it was, with active filters still shown
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. At least one filter is selected (for example two statuses) and the filter bar has been collapsed with the funnel button.
steps: 1. Click the funnel icon in the toolbar again.
2. Look at the filter bar.
expected: 1. The filter bar reappears below the tab row.
2. The previously selected filters are still shown on their chips in the active (blue) state - nothing was lost while collapsed.
3. The 'Clear filters' link is still shown at the right end of the chip row.

title: The collapsed or expanded state of the filter bar is remembered after leaving and returning
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page and have collapsed the filter bar with the funnel button.
steps: 1. Navigate to another page (for example open a work order, or go to Customers).
2. Return to the Work Orders page.
3. Look at the filter bar area.
4. Expand the bar with the funnel button, leave the page again and come back.
expected: 1. After step 2 the filter bar is still collapsed (your choice was remembered).
2. After step 4 the filter bar is expanded again when you return - whichever state you left it in is restored.

title: The funnel button shows a blue indicator when filters are active while the bar is collapsed, and none when no filters are active
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. With NO filters selected, collapse the filter bar with the funnel button and look at the funnel icon.
2. Expand the bar, select at least one filter value (for example a status).
3. Collapse the bar again and look at the funnel icon.
expected: 1. After step 1 the funnel icon shows no special indicator (only its normal pressed look).
2. After step 3 the funnel icon shows a visual indicator (filters icon in primary blue) signalling that active filters are in effect while the bar is hidden.
notes: The exact indicator styling (blue icon vs a dot/badge) - VIU-confirm against the build; the design shows the funnel in the active blue treatment.

title: Active filters keep filtering the table while the filter bar is collapsed
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in several statuses; a Status filter is applied (for example Estimate only) and the table is visibly filtered.
steps: 1. Collapse the filter bar with the funnel button.
2. Look at the work order table.
expected: 1. The table content does not change when the bar collapses - it still shows only the work orders matching the active filters.
2. Hiding the bar only hides the chips; it does not remove or pause the filtering.

title: Imported works alone: picking it greys out the other filters
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (filter lists are role-independent per Branko Round-2 Q3=A).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Imported work orders exist, plus some normal work orders.
3. You are on the Work Orders page, All tab, no filters applied.
steps: 1. Open the Status filter and tick Imported.
2. Look at the other filter chips (Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site).
3. Try to combine Imported with another status.
4. Untick Imported.
expected: 1. The table switches to showing imported work orders only.
2. While Imported is ticked, the other filter chips are greyed out and cannot be used.
3. Imported cannot be combined with other statuses - selecting it works alone.
4. Unticking Imported re-enables the other chips and the normal list returns.
spec_ref: Filters (no Jira epic) (S2-R7 (Imported cannot be combined with anything else; other filter chips disabled while it is active); S2-N4 (the combination is prevented rather than returning an empty result)) [spec v1.6 2026-07-28]
notes: Traceability repaired 2026-07-31 (closing-authenticity pass defect (a)): refs re-pointed from "tech plan G1; spec S2-R1 (conflict raised with the author - export of spec v1.3 awaited)" to the ratified anchors S2-R7 + S2-N4. The conflict is RESOLVED - spec v1.6 (Confluence page 572030978 version 12 2026-07-28) added S2-R7 verbatim: "Imported is an exception to S2-R2 and cannot be combined with anything else ... selecting Imported switches the list to the imported records and disables the other filter chips while it is active. Deselecting Imported returns the list and re-enables the other chips" - which is exactly what this case asserts, so the PENDING-BRANKO question is closed. Tech plan 2026-07-29 G1 independently corroborates the same build behaviour. Exact disabled look/tooltip still VIU-confirm. A saved or shared state combining Imported with other filters must also normalise back to Imported-only on load (tech plan risk 4).
